newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan expected to tender for 108,000T soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan expected to tender for 108,000T soybeans.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 108,000 tonnes of soybeans this week while corn buyers are seen stuck on the sidelines, local traders said on Monday.
A dip in soybean futures prices last week prompted buyers to speed up their purchases, the dealers said.
"Buyers are entering the (soybean) market since soybean prices have fallen sharply from their recent highs," a soybean purchaser said.
The Taiwanese would prefer to buy South American soybeans if the price is between US$5-$10 a tonne lower than U.S. origin, traders said.

Taiwan's Breakfast Soybeans Procurement Association Kaohsiung division will tender on Tuesday for 54,000 tonnes of South American soybeans, traders said. Delivery is for July 1-20 from a Brazilian or Argentinian port.
A successful tender may lure other Taiwanese soy buyers into the market, particularly the unaffiliated Taichung division of the Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group late last week bought a combined shipment comprising 38,000 tonnes of soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of corn through private negotiations with Cargill, traders said. The likely origin for the soybeans and corn is predicted to be either Brazil or Argentina.

No corn tender was expected this week as feed producers continue to reduce inventories following a crippling outbreak of foot and mouth disease, which forced Taiwan to slaughter up to four million of its 14 million pigs, traders said.
Freight rates from the U.S. Pacific Northwest were seen at about US$11.50 a tonne while rates from the Gulf of Mexico fetched a quote of $21.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
